device.description: 12-bit dual-channel ultralow-glitch voltage-output DAC with 50 MHz SPI interface, per-channel references, IOVDD level shifters, daisy-chain SDO and asynchronous clear (power-on zero scale)
device.note: dac7552.pdf (SLAS442D) p.3 power requirements (VDD, IOVDD 2.7-5.5 V; IOVDD down to 1.8 V, note 3), p.4 timing characteristics and serial write operation (Figure 1), p.5 pin description (RGT) and terminal functions, p.13 serial interface programming (Table 1) and power-down mode control (Table 2), p.14 power-on reset (zero scale), p.15 asynchronous clear, serial interface (DCEN low: word executes after the 16th SCLK falling edge)

pages: p.3 (supplies, logic), p.4 (timing, Figure 1), p.5 (pins), p.13 (Tables 1-2), p.14 (power-on reset), p.15 (clear, IOVDD, serial interface, daisy chain)
notModeled: analog outputs, references and VFB sense inputs (never driven)
power-down output loads: stored per channel in PWR only; how a powered-down channel returns to normal operation is not described
PD pin (pin 7, 'power-down'): function and polarity not described in the datasheet; a plain input
daisy-chain mode (DCEN high): SDO repeating SDIN with a 16-clock delay and latching the last 16 bits at SYNC rising are not modeled; SDO stays Hi-Z (the DCEN-low behavior)
DCEN low: the word executes on the 16th SCLK falling edge (commit now); a SYNC rise before it discards the word
CLR resets all registers and the DAC updates at the first SYNC rising edge after CLR returns high: modeled as an immediate clear to code 0
SCLK limits (50 MHz, 10 MHz with SDO) and setup/hold times
variants: DAC7553 (dac7553.pdf) is the same chip with two's complement input coding and mid-scale power-on/clear; own spec file. Daisy-chainable with DAC7551/DAC7558.
